modules.name: Layer manifest, provenance and policy-source register
modules.design_question: What single manifest lets any module find, verify, cache, credit, licence-check and datum-check a layer, and trace every value and clause to a hashed source built by public code?
modules.method: Extend Vista's release-manifest (per-file bytes, sha256) into manifest.json 'vcm-layers/1' with a JSON Schema. Per layer: id, theme, version; source {publisher, dataset_id, url, retrieved, source_modified, data_owner[]}; licence {id, version, url, accessed, attribution, redistribution}; crs {horizontal {epsg, realisation, epoch}, vertical[] {column, datum, epsg|null, epoch, z_offset_m, basis}}; geometry; lod; accuracy; vintage; bbox; count; fields; files [{path, role, format, bytes, sha256, content_type, range_safe, store {release_tag, asset}}]; derived_from; build {script, repo, commit}; modules_using; disclaimer_required; status. Licence id is SPDX where listed, else LicenseRef-*; CI derives share_alike. Only manifest.json has a fixed path. A policy_sources register holds URL, retrieved, bytes, sha256, pages, approved, amended, last_modified_header and etag per PDF or report; any hash change needs a person's reading. Root LICENSE (MIT or Apache-2.0) covers code only; REUSE.toml plus LICENSES/ maps data paths. CI rejects: missing licence, datum or CRS; hash, byte or path mismatch; file over cap; unmapped data path; ODbL ancestor without share_alike; range_safe without a browser probe; GeoParquet '-dev' metadata; build.script absent from a public repo at the recorded commit; templates lacking the unofficial-estimate text. First commit: LICENSE, REUSE.toml, corrected Vista credit. GPT-6 Astra drafts code and text only.
modules.effort: est. 4-5 days (team estimate); LICENSE, REUSE.toml and the Vista credit fix are the first commit
modules.human_judgment: Decide core-bundle layers; MIT or Apache-2.0; attribution and datum wording per publisher; tracked policy documents; whether Vista's supplied-model export stays online until the supplier answers.

modules.name: Storage formats and tiling
modules.design_question: Which format and tiling per layer minimises bytes yet lets the browser load only what the current view needs, while keeping absolute heights for cone tests?
modules.method: Choose format by access pattern. Points and tables (trees, heritage, stations, parcel and tax attributes): GeoParquet 1.1, explicit geometry column, crs as 2D PROJJSON, bbox covering column, Hilbert sort, zstd; read with hyparquet, passing byteLength from the manifest. Display polygons (parcels, footprints, zoning, parks): PMTiles v3 MVT, about z10-z16 with overzoom, plus the same data as GeoParquet for analysis. LOD1: dissolve City outlines split at parcel lines; store a 2D footprint (EPSG:3157, 0.1 m) with absolute elevation columns z_ground_m, z_roof_max_m, z_roof_p50_m, vintage and flags, never baked meshes. Declare each elevation column's datum, EPSG and z_offset_m in the manifest and in a footer key-value entry; use a compound CRS only for true-Z geometry. Derive height_m = z_roof - z_ground for display; MapLibre fill-extrusion takes height and base in metres. Mark LOD1.3 where tops differ by about 2 m. Terrain and canopy rasters: uint16 decimetres or uint8 half-metres as WebP/PNG tiles in PMTiles, or COG. Meshes: glTF with KHR_mesh_quantization and EXT_meshopt_compression. 3D Tiles only if Cesium is adopted (ellipsoidal heights). View cones: analytic parameters, not meshes. Point clouds: link NRCan COPC, never mirror. OSM-derived tiles are a separate ODbL layer. Measure sizes before committing any layer.
modules.human_judgment: Choose which layers need analysis-grade geometry (Parquet) versus display-only tiles; accept lossy simplification for far context buildings; set the change-detection threshold for 2015 footprints.

modules.name: GitHub hosting, durable store, size budgets and range/compression
modules.design_question: How do we host a multi-layer open dataset within GitHub limits, keep a durable copy of every built layer, and keep range-read formats working in every target browser?
modules.method: Limits (docs): Pages site 1 GB, 10-minute deploy timeout, soft 100 GB/month; the 10 builds/hour limit does not apply to custom Actions workflows; no free hosting of a commercial SaaS. Git warns at 50 MiB, blocks at 100 MiB; releases 2 GiB per file, 1,000 assets, no CORS; LFS unusable with Pages. Store of record: one GitHub release per layer version (tag layers/<id>/<sha12>), created as a draft, assets attached, then published with release immutability on. CI restores current and previous files from releases (gh release download), verifies sha256, assembles the site, uploads the Pages artifact and deploys. A failed portal fetch keeps the last released version, flagged stale; rollback is a redeploy of an earlier manifest. Pages artifacts (1 day default), Actions artifacts (90 days default) and caches (7 days idle) are never the store of record. Measured 21 Oct 2026: Pages max-age=600, ACAO *, no Access-Control-Expose-Headers; Chromium 152 sends identity with Range (206, raw size); browser HEAD returns the gzip length. Probe every extension in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit with Playwright; pass byteLength from the manifest; fallback: 1 km shards or a CORS object store.
modules.effort: est. 3-4 days including Playwright probes and the release-store workflow
modules.human_judgment: If Firefox or WebKit probes fail, choose sharding or a CORS object store (adds an account and cost). If VCM is ever monetised, move off Pages. Decide how many versions per layer to keep.

modules.name: Local cache and layer subscription
modules.design_question: How do tools subscribe to layers, stay fresh as open data and policy change, and work offline with minimal bandwidth, without colliding with other apps on the shared origin?
modules.method: Subscription is manifest plus versions. The client fetches manifest.json (Pages caches it 10 minutes), compares each layer version and sha256 with its cache, and downloads only changed content-addressed files. Browser cache: Cache Storage or OPFS under vcm/layers/<id>/<sha>, current and previous kept; call navigator.storage.persist(). All four team sites share the origin ruijieliu6.github.io, so every cache name, key and OPFS path carries the vcm prefix, and VCM data is served from that same origin (Content-Range stays readable). Desktop/Python: LOCALAPPDATA/vancouver-context/layer/version/ with a lock file. Modules call registry.require and receive a handle plus attribution; they re-render on layer-updated. A weekly Action rebuilds a layer only when the portal modified stamp changes AND the sha256 of the normalised export changes; data_processed is not a trigger. Scheduled workflows are disabled after 60 days without repository activity in a public repo: add a keep-alive and workflow_dispatch. Policy PDFs return 403 to non-browser clients and the Terms of Use list repeated automated access as overburdening conduct: re-hashing is a person's browser step recorded by pull request, saving Last-Modified and ETag, with an optional tolerant HEAD. Offline mode serves cached layers with source dates.

modules.name: Licence, attribution, non-endorsement and share-alike
modules.design_question: Which licence, attribution and disclaimer does each layer carry, how do we stop ODbL share-alike spreading, and which inherited Vista assets may enter the base?
modules.method: Licence register keyed by layer, ids SPDX or LicenseRef-*. (1) Code: root LICENSE (MIT or Apache-2.0) in all four repos as the first commit; none exists; data stays under per-layer licences via manifest and REUSE.toml. (2) OGL-Vancouver v1.0, OGL-Metro Vancouver, OGL-BC 2.0, OGL-Canada 2.0: attribution plus licence link; no official status, no City name, crest or logo. (3) City guidelines and council reports are City copyright, non-commercial copying with Terms-of-Use notice: store transcribed numbers and citations only. (4) OSM and Overture are ODbL: separate files, share_alike, no OSM-City merges, Overture kept out of the city extent; OSM tiles obey the tile policy (no bulk or offline), so form-studio's tile.openstreetmap.org use needs replacing. (5) TransLink GTFS: limited, revocable redistribution with legend and indemnity; outside the open bundle. (6) BC Assessment bulk is not open; the City tax report is co-owned. (7) Vista: credit the central model as OSM-derived now; do not inherit the supplied-model export, terrain, water or shoreline until supplier permission and an ODbL classification exist; otherwise rebuild from City footprints, LiDAR and class 5 water. (8) Every warning, surface and export carries: Unofficial estimate, not a City of Vancouver determination. NOTICE and footers are generated from lineage.
modules.human_judgment: Obtain the supplier's written permission and an ODbL classification for the studio model, or drop it; decide whether to unpublish Vista's model export meanwhile; ask the City and Metro Vancouver about attribution and BC Assessment co-owned fields; choose MIT or Apache-2.0.

modules.name: Vertical datum, CRS registry and cone-test uncertainty
modules.design_question: How do heights from CGVD28, CGVD28GVRD, CGVD2013, EGM96 and ellipsoid layers, and portal lon/lat labelled WGS84, stay comparable, and how is the remaining error carried into a cone or airspace test?
modules.method: Every z-bearing file declares z_ref, vertical epoch and horizontal realisation. Known: City LiDAR 2013 CGVD28; 2018 and 2022 CGVD28GVRD (HTMVBC00 geoid), horizontal NAD83(CSRS) 4.0.0.BC.1.GVRD; NRCan HRDEM CGVD2013 in EPSG:3979; Vista SRTM EGM96; 3D Tiles ellipsoid; cone heights 'geodetic', datum unnamed. EPSG: 5713 CGVD28; CGVD2013a 9245 (2010, NAD83(CSRS) v6/v7), 20034 (2002, v4), 20035 (1997, v2/v3); 4979; 3157; 4617; 3005. Match the CGVD2013a epoch to each layer's horizontal version (City LiDAR 'v4' suggests 20034, unconfirmed). Portal lon/lat equal NAD83(CSRS) values; mixing with GNSS, imagery or 3D Tiles needs a declared transform. Estimate z_offset_m by differencing HRDEM VILLE_VANCOUVER (2013-02-19) against City 2013 LiDAR on bare ground; +0.15 m is a placeholder. Cone test: massing tolerance 0 m (cl. 3.1.1). margin = z_limit - z_top; U = root-sum-square of datum, LiDAR, footprint and user-declared georeference errors; result clear (margin >= U), within_uncertainty, or encroaches (margin <= -U), always labelled unofficial. If the lower-boundary model is unconfirmed, compute every candidate and show the spread. Reference-roof cones use LiDAR roof elevations in LiDAR's own datum.
modules.effort: est. 3-4 days including the offset study
modules.human_judgment: Confirm with the City which datum cone geodetic heights use, whether 'measured from' a corner means elevation or height above that corner's ground, and the NAD83(CSRS) epoch of City LiDAR; set the user-model georeference error entry.

modules.name: Trees and canopy layers
modules.design_question: How do we store street trees and canopy compactly while stating height and crown uncertainty honestly, mode by mode?
modules.method: Trees: build cov-public-trees from the portal Parquet export (10,358,425 B raw). Keep asset_id, genus/species dictionary ids, diameter_cm (uint16, 0.1 cm), height_m, height_mode and position (0.1 m, EPSG:3157). height_mode: ft_class (ten values 4.6-32.0 m = 15-105 ft in 10 ft steps; 176,200 trees, 95.62%), metre_value (whole or half metres; 8,032, 4.36%), other (36), suspect (40 m or more: 11 trees, plus any height above the LiDAR canopy at that point plus a margin). Label ft_class 'recorded class value (inferred 10 ft bins)', about +/-1.5 m; no uncertainty claimed for other modes; exclude suspect from shadow studies by default. Drop or flag 477 zero diameters, 3 zero heights and 1 null geometry. Crown width is not supplied: estimate from diameter and genus (team assumption; calibrate on LiDAR). Canopy: derive a canopy height model from City LiDAR 2022 (class 4, DSM minus DTM) at 2 m, uint8 half-metre tiles; 2013 and 2018 give change checks; Metro Vancouver 2020 (5 m) and 2014 (2 m LiDAR) land cover are regional cross-checks. Private trees exist only in the CHM. Prototype: 184,267 valid trees pack to 874,891 B (4.75 B each) with zlib-9.
